title: Every finite-dimensional irreducible universal Racah module over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field is one of the explicit bidiagonal R_d(a,b,c) modules
author: Hau-Wen Huang; Sarah Bockting-Conrad
work: Finite-Dimensional Irreducible Modules of the Racah Algebra at Characteristic Zero
source_version: Official SIGMA 16 (2020) article 018, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2020.018; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs cyclic bases using spectral endpoints without assuming the Racah generators diagonalizable. It controls the resulting triangular operators by the defining quadratic commutator relations and proves that the superdiagonal coefficients obey a uniquely determined second-difference recurrence. The universal infinite-dimensional module and its polynomial quotient then identify every irreducible module with the explicit model, overcoming the semisimplicity failure illustrated in the paper.

The PBW basis theorem is explicitly cited prior background. Proposition2.4/3.1 supplies complete operator matrices and coefficients and leaves their defining-relation verification as routine computations; this is retained as bounded author-supported verification, not an omitted new classification core. Select6.3 only, not a separate irreducibility criterion, parameter-orbit bijection or diagonalizability claim. retained_original_metadata.statement_scope: Full Theorem6.3 for the universal Racah algebra R of Definition2.1, F algebraically closed of characteristic zero, d a nonnegative integer, and V any irreducible R-module of dimension d+1. There exist a,b,c in F with V isomorphic to the explicitly defined R_d(a,b,c) of Proposition2.4. No diagonalizability of A,B,C is assumed, and no uniqueness of the parameter triple is asserted.
